title: Homology pairing of Cech totals preserving both axes
statement: For any scheme $X$, family of opens $U_i$, modules $F,G$, computing resolution pairing $D$ [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data], and $p,q\ge0$, there exists a $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$-bilinear map $t:H^p(A)\times H^q(B)\to H^{p+q}(C)$ for the three Cech totals [def-sc-cup-cech-total]. It carries the alpha classes of two global resolution cocycles to the alpha class of their D-paired cocycle. It carries the beta classes of two coefficient Cech cocycles to the beta class of their Alexander-Whitney cup cocycle [def-sc-cech-cup-product]. Both assertions use the concrete underlying-cochain equalities; no covering or flasque hypothesis occurs.

source.place: Tag 07MB and 0FKV; homology descent of the signed cochain pairing

proof.text: Obtain the signed total cochain morphism h and its two axis formulas.

For any two nonnegative complexes over a commutative ring, the tensor differential formula shows the tensor-summand image of two cocycles is a cocycle. Lift it uniquely through the cycle inclusion. Currying its homology class gives a bilinear map on cycles. A first-input boundary has primitive given by tensoring its primitive with the second cocycle. A second-input boundary has primitive multiplied by the inverse of the tensor sign. When either input degree is zero its incoming differential is zero, so this boundary assertion holds without a negative-degree primitive. Thus the bilinear map annihilates both boundary submodules. Descend once in each variable using ShortComplex.descHomology; epimorphic homology projections prove linearity after the second descent. This entire nonnegative tensor-homology argument is proved by the private helpers in the module.

Postcompose the tensor homology pairing with H(h). Naturality of homology projections and injectivity of the target cycle inclusion identify the class of any cycle whose underlying cochain is the h-image of the pure tensor. Apply this to cycles mapped through alpha, and then through beta. cyclesMap_i and homologyπ_naturality identify their inclusions and classes, and the two cochain equations of h give the stated formulas.

theorem exists_cupCech_total_pairing {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u}
    (U : ι → X.Opens) {F G : X.Modules} (D : CupResolutionPairing F G) (p q : ℕ) :
    ∃ t : ((cupCechDouble U D.left.K).total (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).homology p →ₗ[Γ(X, ⊤)]
      ((cupCechDouble U D.right.K).total (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).homology q →ₗ[Γ(X, ⊤)]
      ((cupCechDouble U D.target.K).total (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).homology (p + q),
      (∀ (a : ((cupSections D.left).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (b : ((cupSections D.right).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (c : ((cupSections D.target).sc (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        c.val = D.pair p q ⊤ a.val b.val →
        t (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (cupCechAlpha U D.left) p (cupCycleClass _ p a))
          (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (cupCechAlpha U D.right) q (cupCycleClass _ q b)) =
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (cupCechAlpha U D.target) (p + q)
          (cupCycleClass _ (p + q) c)) ∧
      (∀ (a : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj F.presheafModuleCat).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (b : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj G.presheafModuleCat).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (c : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj (F ⊗ G).presheafModuleCat).sc
          (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        c.val = cechCupCochain U F G p q a.val b.val →
        t (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (cupCechBeta U D.left) p (cupCycleClass _ p a))
          (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (cupCechBeta U D.right) q (cupCycleClass _ q b)) =
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (cupCechBeta U D.target) (p + q)
          (cupCycleClass _ (p + q) c))
